title: Arrearage Management Program Rules — Forgiveness of Scheduled Installments
content:
# Arrearage Management Program Rules — Forgiveness of Scheduled Installments

## Rules in force

1. In an Arrearage Management Program plan, the forgiveness kind of Payment Arrangement, each scheduled installment is forgiven instead of billed when the current charges of the bill that carries it are paid in full by that bill's due date.
2. When the current bill is not paid in full by its due date, the forgiveness for that installment is withheld. Where the kind restores withheld forgiveness, it is posted once that bill is paid in full, as long as the plan is still active and no default has occurred.
3. Each installment number is forgiven at most once and is never both forgiven and billed.
4. Forgiveness is posted only on a plan in active status.
5. The customer's total forgiveness is limited by the program's per-customer cap.
6. Repayment plans never forgive.

A forgiveness entry takes the forgiven amount out of the plan balance and records the scheduled installment forgiven and the service bill whose on-time payment earned it.

## Retired rule

The former rule that the forgiveness is the kind's forgiveness share of the scheduled installment and is posted under the kind's posting term is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis. Under the current basis, an installment forgiven because the current charges of its bill were paid in full by that bill's due date is forgiven at the kind's forgiveness share of the scheduled installment and posted under the kind's posting term.

## Truth table for one scheduled installment

| Current charges of the carrying bill paid in full by its due date | Plan active, no default | Installment already forgiven or billed | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | No | Forgiven instead of billed |
| No | Yes | No | Forgiveness withheld |
| No, later paid in full | Yes | No | Withheld forgiveness posted once the bill is paid in full |
| Any | Yes | Yes | Not forgiven again |
| Any | No — plan not active | Any | No forgiveness posted |

title: Payment Arrangement Schedule A — Arrangement Kinds and Entry Requirements
content:
# Payment Arrangement Schedule A — Arrangement Kinds and Entry Requirements

Lakeshore Power & Light offers seven kinds of Payment Arrangement. Each kind is open only to the customer class and on the bases shown below; a kind is enrolled only where every requirement in its row is met on the enrollment date.

## A.1 Customer class, hardship bases and season

| Arrangement kind | Customer class | Hardship basis required | Active budget billing plan on the same agreement required | Electric space heating required | Senior basis (minimum age of the residential account holder) | Current income qualification required | Enrollment window |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Payment Extension | Residential or business | No | No | No | None (0) | No | Any time |
| Short-Term Installment Plan | Residential | No | No | No | None (0) | No | Any time |
| Standard Deferred Payment Agreement | Residential | No | No | No | None (0) | No | Any time |
| Extended Deferred Payment Agreement | Residential | Yes | Yes | No | None (0) | No | Any time |
| Winter Protection Plan | Residential | No | No | Yes | 65 | No | 11-01 through 03-31 |
| Arrearage Management Program | Residential | No | No | No | None (0) | Yes | Any time |
| Commercial Deferred Payment Agreement | Business | No | No | No | None (0) | No | Any time |

A hardship basis is either an active medical certification on the agreement or a current income qualification. For the Winter Protection Plan the senior basis and a current income qualification are alternatives: the plan needs electric space heating and either of the two. A senior age of 0 means the kind has no senior basis.

## A.2 Arrears age, service length, disconnection and channel

| Arrangement kind | Minimum age of the oldest unpaid bill past its due date | Minimum months since the agreement's start date | May be enrolled on a disconnected agreement | Online self-service enrollment without an agent |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Payment Extension | 0 days (no minimum) | 0 (no minimum) | No | Yes |
| Short-Term Installment Plan | 0 days (no minimum) | 0 (no minimum) | Yes | Yes |
| Standard Deferred Payment Agreement | 0 days (no minimum) | 0 (no minimum) | Yes | No |
| Extended Deferred Payment Agreement | 0 days (no minimum) | 0 (no minimum) | Yes | No |
| Winter Protection Plan | 0 days (no minimum) | 0 (no minimum) | Yes | No |
| Arrearage Management Program | 90 days | 6 | No | No |
| Commercial Deferred Payment Agreement | 0 days (no minimum) | 6 | Yes | No |

## Notes to Schedule A

- A kind marked "No" for a disconnected agreement is available only while the agreement is active or under a pending disconnection notice.
- The enrollment window is a calendar window by month and day; the Winter Protection Plan accepts enrollment from November 1 through March 31, both days included, and every other kind at any time of the year.
- Self-service enrollment refers to the customer enrolling through online self-service without an agent; the kinds marked "No" are set up through an agent.

## Illustrations (hypothetical customers)

| Hypothetical customer | Kinds the class and bases in this schedule leave open |
|---|---|
| Business customer, agreement started 4 months ago | Payment Extension only (the Commercial Deferred Payment Agreement needs 6 months) |
| Residential customer aged 67, electric space heating, enrolling on December 10 | The Winter Protection Plan among others |
| Residential customer aged 67, gas space heating | Not the Winter Protection Plan |
| Residential customer with a current income qualification, oldest unpaid bill 60 days past due | Not the Arrearage Management Program (90 days required) |

title: Payment Arrangement Terms — Waiver, Deferred Amount, Installment Count and Due Dates
content:
# Payment Arrangement Terms — Waiver, Deferred Amount, Installment Count and Due Dates

This rule sets the terms recorded when a Payment Arrangement is enrolled: the treatment of the down payment for income-qualified customers, the deferred amount, the installment count and amount, the down payment due date and the date of a Payment Extension's single installment.

## Terms in force

1. **Income-qualification waiver.** When the kind waives the down payment for income-qualified customers and the customer's income qualification is current on the enrollment date, the down payment is waived and recorded as zero, with the plan marked as waived.
2. **Deferred amount.** The deferred amount is the eligible balance less the down payment.
3. **Installment count.** The installment count chosen by the customer is reduced, one at a time, until the regular installment reaches the kind's smallest installment, but never below the kind's fewest installments. A balance that cannot meet the smallest installment at the fewest installments is not placed in that kind of plan.
4. **Installment amount.** The regular installment is the deferred amount divided by the count, rounded down to the cent, and the final installment carries the remainder.
5. **Down payment due date.** The down payment is due the kind's days to pay, in calendar days, after enrollment.
6. **Payment Extension date.** For a Payment Extension the single installment is billed on the extended due date, which is chosen by the customer and lies no more than the longest extension, in calendar days, after the enrollment date.

## Retired terms

- The former definition of the eligible balance — the past-due balance of the agreement on the enrollment date (bills past their due date plus posted charges, less payments and credits) for kinds measured on the past-due balance, the whole account balance for kinds measured on the total balance, capped for Arrearage Management Program plans by the customer's remaining forgiveness room — is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis.
- The former down payment formula — the eligible balance times the kind's down payment share, or its disconnected share when the agreement is disconnected at enrollment, rounded to the cent and raised to the kind's minimum down payment, never more than the eligible balance, and zero for kinds with a zero share — is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis.

## Current basis — plans other than a Payment Extension under disconnection notice

For every plan other than a Payment Extension on a residential agreement whose status is disconnection notice pending:

- **Eligible balance.** The eligible balance is the past-due balance of the service agreement on the enrollment date (bills past their due date plus posted charges, less payments and credits) for kinds measured on the past-due balance, and the whole account balance for kinds measured on the total balance, capped for Arrearage Management Program plans by the customer's remaining forgiveness room.
- **Down payment.** The down payment is the eligible balance times the kind's down payment share, or times its disconnected share when the agreement is disconnected at enrollment, rounded to the cent and raised to the kind's minimum down payment, but never more than the eligible balance; it is zero for kinds whose down payment share is zero.

| Hypothetical plan | Eligible balance | Share applied | Share of the balance | Minimum | Down payment |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Short-Term Installment Plan, connected | $640.00 | 30% | $192.00 | $50.00 | $192.00 |
| Short-Term Installment Plan, disconnected at enrollment | $640.00 | 50% | $320.00 | $50.00 | $320.00 |
| Short-Term Installment Plan, connected | $120.00 | 30% | $36.00 | $50.00 | $50.00, raised to the minimum |
| Commercial Deferred Payment Agreement, connected | $500.00 | 33% | $165.00 | $250.00 | $250.00, raised to the minimum |
| Winter Protection Plan | $900.00 | 0% | — | — | Zero |

Where the income-qualification waiver applies, the down payment is recorded as zero whatever the table gives.

## Worked terms (hypothetical plans)

**Count reduction.** A Standard Deferred Payment Agreement carries a deferred amount of $130.00 and the customer chooses 6 installments; the kind's smallest installment is $25.00 and its fewest installments 4.

| Count tried | Deferred amount divided by the count, rounded down | Reaches $25.00 |
|---|---|---|
| 6 | $21.66 | No |
| 5 | $26.00 | Yes — count fixed at 5 |

Result: 5 installments with a regular installment of $26.00; the final installment carries the remainder, which here is also $26.00.

**Balance too small.** A deferred amount of $90.00 on the same kind gives $22.50 at 4 installments, below $25.00 at the fewest count; the balance is not placed in that kind of plan.

**Payment Extension date.** Enrolled on October 3 with a longest extension of 14 days, the customer may choose an extended due date up to and including October 17.

title: Arrearage Management Program Autopay Credit Schedule
content:
# Arrearage Management Program Autopay Credit Schedule

**Schedule.** When withheld forgiveness on a program bill of an Arrearage Management Program plan, the forgiveness kind of Payment Arrangement, is posted as a catch-up, the autopay credit is set by the autopay payments posted to the Electric Service Agreement within the 6 months before the posting:

| Autopay payments posted within the 6 months | Autopay credit |
|---|---|
| 5 or more | 10% |
| At least 1 but fewer than 5 | 5% |
| None | 0 |

The payments counted are the Electric Service Agreement's payments whose channel is autopay. A window of 6 months before the posting covers payments posted after the same calendar day 6 months earlier, up to and including the posting date.

## Boundary readings (hypothetical)

| Autopay payments in the window | 0 | 1 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Autopay credit | 0 | 5% | 5% | 10% | 10% |

title: Payment Arrangement Balance Limits and Care-Desk Approval Authority
content:
# Payment Arrangement Balance Limits and Care-Desk Approval Authority

For every kind of Payment Arrangement the company fixes the smallest and the largest balance the kind takes, the basis on which that balance is measured, and the largest deferred amount a customer care agent may approve; larger deferred amounts go to the credit department.

| Arrangement kind | Smallest eligible balance | Largest eligible balance | Balance basis | Largest deferred amount a customer care agent may approve |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Payment Extension | $25.00 | $1500.00 | Past-due balance | $1500.00 |
| Short-Term Installment Plan | $100.00 | $1000.00 | Past-due balance | $1000.00 |
| Standard Deferred Payment Agreement | $200.00 | $3000.00 | Past-due balance | $3000.00 |
| Extended Deferred Payment Agreement | $200.00 | $6000.00 | Past-due balance | $6000.00 |
| Winter Protection Plan | $1.00 | $5000.00 | Past-due balance | $5000.00 |
| Arrearage Management Program | $500.00 | $8000.00 | Past-due balance | $8000.00 |
| Commercial Deferred Payment Agreement | $500.00 | $25000.00 | Total balance | $10000.00 |

## Balance bases

- **Past-due balance**: the bills of the service agreement that are past their due date, together with its charges.
- **Total balance**: the whole account balance of the service agreement.

Only the Commercial Deferred Payment Agreement is measured on the total balance; the six other kinds are measured on the past-due balance.

## Reading the authority column

For six kinds the care-desk approval limit equals the largest eligible balance of the kind. For the Commercial Deferred Payment Agreement the two differ: the kind accepts a balance of up to $25000.00, but a customer care agent may approve a deferred amount of no more than $10000.00.

| Hypothetical deferred amount | Kind | Within the care-desk approval limit |
|---|---|---|
| $1500.00 | Payment Extension | Yes (equal to the limit) |
| $1500.01 | Payment Extension | No |
| $9800.00 | Commercial Deferred Payment Agreement | Yes |
| $12000.00 | Commercial Deferred Payment Agreement | No — above $10000.00 |

title: Remittance Standard — Booking-Day Customer Payments on Arrearage Management Program Bills
content:
# Remittance Standard — Booking-Day Customer Payments on Arrearage Management Program Bills

**Standard.** When a program bill of an Arrearage Management Program plan, the forgiveness kind of Payment Arrangement, is booked as missed, the recognised customer booking-day payments are:

1. the customer payments posted on the booking day through an authorized pay station, whose receipts post the business day after they are taken, and by mailed check, whose postmark is honoured — when no returned-payment charge was posted to the Electric Service Agreement within the returned-payment look-back of its rate schedule;
2. the pay-station payments alone — when at least one returned-payment charge but fewer than the rate schedule's returned-payment restriction count were posted within that look-back, since a mailed check from such an agreement is recognised only once it has cleared;
3. zero — when the restriction count was reached, since an agreement under the returned-payment restriction is given no posting courtesy.

A card, online or autopay payment posted on the booking day was made after the cure period and is never recognised.

The look-back and the restriction count are those of the rate schedule of the Electric Service Agreement; the payments read are the Electric Service Agreement's payments posted on the booking day and the channel each came through.

## Decision table (hypothetical booking day: $50.00 at an authorized pay station, $30.00 mailed check, $20.00 by card)

| Returned-payment charges within the rate schedule's look-back | Recognised customer booking-day payments |
|---|---|
| None | $80.00 (pay station and mailed check) |
| At least one, fewer than the restriction count | $50.00 (pay station alone) |
| Restriction count reached | $0.00 |

The $20.00 card payment is never recognised.

title: Arrearage Management Program Catch-Up Forgiveness Amount — Calculation Memo
content:
# Arrearage Management Program Catch-Up Forgiveness Amount — Calculation Memo

This memorandum sets the amount of a catch-up forgiveness posted on an Arrearage Management Program plan, the forgiveness kind of Payment Arrangement.

## 1. The amount

The catch-up forgiveness is the scheduled installment times the catch-up share, never more than the remaining forgiveness room, rounded half-up to the cent.

## 2. The scheduled installment

The scheduled installment is the plan's remaining balance when the installment is the last one of the plan not yet forgiven or billed — that is, when the forgiveness entries and installment billings on the plan together number one less than its installment count — and otherwise the plan's regular installment amount, but never more than its remaining balance.

## 3. The catch-up share

The catch-up share is one, less the lateness cut and less the late-charge cut, plus the progress credit and plus the autopay credit; these are first added together into one share, which is then held between zero and one before it is applied once to the scheduled installment. The standard catch-up share is one, so that the whole scheduled installment is forgiven. The days late are counted, as standard, from the bill's due date to the date it was paid in full.

## 4. The remaining forgiveness room

The remaining forgiveness room is the program's lifetime forgiveness cap per customer less the forgiveness already posted on the plan, the customer's forgiveness on earlier program plans having already limited the plan's balance when it was enrolled.

## Worked memo (hypothetical 12-installment plan, program cap $8000.00)

| Line | Plan A | Plan B | Plan C |
|---|---|---|---|
| Regular installment amount | $187.25 | $187.25 | $187.25 |
| Remaining balance | $1310.75 | $187.31 | $1310.75 |
| Forgiveness entries and billings so far | 5 | 11 (one less than 12) | 5 |
| Scheduled installment | $187.25 | $187.31, the remaining balance | $187.25 |
| Forgiveness already posted on the plan | $3410.00 | $5000.00 | $7900.00 |
| Remaining room | $4590.00 | $3000.00 | $100.00 |
| Catch-up share | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| Catch-up forgiveness | $187.25 | $187.31 | $100.00, held to the room |

title: Arrearage Management Program Catch-Up Forgiveness — Program Operations Card
content:
# Arrearage Management Program Catch-Up Forgiveness — Program Operations Card

**Rule.** Where the forgiveness for a program bill of an Arrearage Management Program plan — the forgiveness kind of Payment Arrangement — was withheld because its current charges were not paid in full by the due date, the withheld forgiveness is posted as a catch-up once that bill is paid in full, on the day it is paid in full, while the plan is active and has not defaulted. The program bill a catch-up is earned on is the agreement's most recent bill. The program's rules on when catch-up is posted, on posting each installment once and on the customer's forgiveness cap are unchanged.

A catch-up forgiveness is not posted until the plan carries a missed-installment entry for the program bill it is earned on wherever that bill was still unpaid when its cure period ended.

## Posting the forgiveness — `post_arrangement_forgiveness_78b684e3`

**What the tool does.** It posts a forgiveness entry for one scheduled installment of an Arrearage Management Program plan. A forgiveness entry dated today is added to the plan's history for the installment number given, linked to the bill whose payment earned it, and the plan's remaining balance is reduced by the amount forgiven. Afterwards the plan history shows the forgiveness and the plan lookup shows the lower remaining balance.

**How it is invoked.** This is an agent-side tool. The agent unlocks it with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool` and then calls it with `call_agent_discoverable_tool`, naming `post_arrangement_forgiveness_78b684e3`.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `arrangement_id` | The reference number of the Arrearage Management Program plan, as returned by the payment arrangement lookup | Identifier |
| `installment_number` | The position of the scheduled installment being forgiven (1 is the first) | Whole number (integer) |
| `bill_id` | The bill reference number of the program bill whose payment earned the forgiveness, as returned by the bill lookup | Identifier |
| `amount` | The amount forgiven | US dollars with 2 decimal places, a plain number such as 140.25 with no currency sign; stored rounded half-up to the cent |

**Return.** A text receipt: "Forgiveness <entry_id> posted on <arrangement_id> for installment <n>: <amount> USD; remaining balance <balance> USD." The entry identifier is the reference number of the new history entry, the installment number is the one given, and both amounts carry 2 decimal places. Receiving this receipt means the forgiveness is posted.

## Illustration (hypothetical values)

A call with `arrangement_id` ARR-0003, `installment_number` 6, `bill_id` BILL-0042 and `amount` 187.25 on a plan holding $1310.75 returns: "Forgiveness <entry_id> posted on ARR-0003 for installment 6: 187.25 USD; remaining balance 1123.50 USD."

title: Payment Arrangement Completion, Cancellation on Closure and Lapse
content:
# Payment Arrangement Completion, Cancellation on Closure and Lapse

**Standard.** A Payment Arrangement plan is completed when its plan balance reaches zero through billed installments that have been paid, forgiveness, or an early payoff, and no installment is left unpaid past its cure period. When the service agreement carrying an active plan closes, the plan moves to the customer's new service agreement where the kind moves with the customer and the customer has opened one; otherwise the plan is cancelled and its remaining balance is returned to the closing agreement, where it becomes part of the final bill. A lapsed plan — one whose down payment was not received — has no balance to return.

## Outcomes by situation

| Situation | Kind moves with the customer | New agreement opened | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| Plan balance reaches zero, no installment unpaid past its cure period | — | — | Completed |
| Agreement carrying an active plan closes | Yes | Yes | Plan moves to the new agreement |
| Agreement carrying an active plan closes | Yes | No | Cancelled; remaining balance returned to the closing agreement's final bill |
| Agreement carrying an active plan closes | No | Any | Cancelled; remaining balance returned to the closing agreement's final bill |
| Down payment not received by its due date | — | — | Lapsed on the day after the due date; nothing to return |

## Hypothetical closure

A customer on an active Arrearage Management Program plan with $1240.00 still under the plan closes the account and opens service at a new address. The program does not move with the customer, so the plan is cancelled and the $1240.00 is returned to the closing agreement, where it becomes part of the final bill.

title: Payment Arrangement Cure Periods, Missed Installments and Default
content:
# Payment Arrangement Cure Periods, Missed Installments and Default

## Rule in force

1. An installment counts as missed only when it is still unpaid after the cure period that follows its due date.
2. The cure period is the kind's cure days, counted in calendar days from the day after the installment's due date, extended by the kind's medical extension days when a medical certification on the agreement is active on the due date. A payment posted on the last cure day is in time.
3. Where the kind requires the current bill to be paid as well, the current charges of each bill carrying an installment are treated the same way, and an unpaid current bill after its cure period is recorded as a missed installment of the installment that bill carries.
4. A missed installment is recorded on the day after the cure period ended, once for each installment number.
5. The plan defaults when the missed installments recorded on it since its latest activation or reinstatement reach the kind's default count. On default the remaining plan balance is returned to the service agreement and is immediately past due, and the disconnection process may start again only with a new written notice.
6. A missed installment that is later paid is not removed from the count, except through reinstatement.

The due date is taken from the service bill that carries the installment.

## Retired clause

The former clause that an installment is paid when payments to the service agreement, applied oldest charges first, cover it, less a shortfall of no more than the kind's tolerance, by the end of its cure period, is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis. Under the current basis, any installment other than one carried by a program bill of an Arrearage Management Program plan, and the current charges of any other bill carrying an installment, are paid when payments to the service agreement, applied oldest charges first, cover them, less a shortfall of no more than the kind's tolerance, by the end of their cure period.

| Hypothetical installment | Covered by payments by the last cure day | Shortfall | Kind's tolerance | Paid |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Standard Deferred Payment Agreement, $158.20 | $157.50 | $0.70 | $1.00 | Yes |
| Standard Deferred Payment Agreement, $158.20 | $157.00 | $1.20 | $1.00 | No |
| Commercial Deferred Payment Agreement, $412.00 | $411.90 | $0.10 | $0.00 | No |

## Calendar cases (hypothetical, cure period of 10 days)

| Due date | Medical certification active on the due date | Extra days | Last cure day | Paid on | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| May 20 | No | 0 | May 30 | May 30 | In time |
| May 20 | No | 0 | May 30 | May 31 | Missed, recorded May 31 |
| May 20 | Yes | 10 | June 9 | June 9 | In time |
| May 20 | Yes | 10 | June 9 | Unpaid | Missed, recorded June 10 |

## Default count (hypothetical Standard Deferred Payment Agreement, default count 2)

| Missed installments recorded since the latest activation or reinstatement | Plan status |
|---|---|
| 1 | Active |
| 2 | Defaulted; remaining balance returned to the agreement and immediately past due |

title: Arrearage Management Program — Counting the Days Late of a Program Bill
content:
# Arrearage Management Program — Counting the Days Late of a Program Bill

**Standard.** For a catch-up forgiveness on an Arrearage Management Program plan, the forgiveness kind of Payment Arrangement, the program bill is the Electric Service Agreement's most recent bill and the date it was paid in full is the posting date of the latest payment posted to the agreement. The point from which its days late are counted is set as follows:

1. When the Electric Service Agreement's start date lies at least 360 whole calendar months before the posting and no returned-payment charge was posted to it within the 24 months before the posting, the days late are counted from the last day of the cure period, that is the due date plus the plan's cure period days.
2. When the start date lies that far back and such a charge was posted within those months, they are counted from the end of the late-payment grace of the agreement's rate schedule, that is the due date plus its late-payment grace days.
3. In every other case they are counted from the due date.

Months between the start date and the posting are counted in whole calendar months. A window of 24 months before the posting covers charges posted after the same calendar day 24 months earlier, up to and including the posting date.

## Worked counts (hypothetical program bill due June 12, paid in full June 25; plan cure period of 10 days; rate schedule late-payment grace of 5 days)

| Electric Service Agreement | Counted from | Days late |
|---|---|---|
| Started 1990, no returned-payment charge in 24 months | June 22, the last cure day | 3 |
| Started 1990, a returned-payment charge 11 months ago | June 17, the end of the grace | 8 |
| Started 2001 | June 12, the due date | 13 |

title: Desk Tool Card — Reinstating a Defaulted Deferred Payment Agreement
content:
# Desk Tool Card — Reinstating a Defaulted Deferred Payment Agreement

**Terms.** A defaulted Standard Deferred Payment Agreement or Extended Deferred Payment Agreement — the two deferred payment agreement kinds of Payment Arrangement — is reinstated at the customer's request on the terms of this card, which refine the reinstatement rule of the Payment Arrangement program; the reinstatement window, the number of reinstatements allowed and the requirement that the request fall inside the window are unchanged.

- On reinstatement the plan returns to active, the missed-installment count restarts from zero, the remaining installments keep their numbers and amounts, and the balance booked back under the plan is the reinstatement re-deferral rather than the whole returned balance.
- For a reinstated deferred payment agreement, the amount booked back into the plan and credited off the service agreement's collectible balance is the reinstatement re-deferral, not the remaining unbilled plan balance.
- Before reinstatement the customer must have paid the kind's required share of all installments recorded as missed and the whole restoration payment, through payments posted to the service agreement after the default.

## Recording the reinstatement — `reinstate_arrangement_7e9638f2`

**What the tool does.** It reinstates one deferred payment agreement (Standard or Extended) that is in default, putting it back into force today. The agreement identified by the reference number is set back to active status with today's date as its latest status change, and the balance held under it is set to the re-deferred amount given, which from then on is the deferred balance repaid by the arrangement's remaining installments. The installment count and the regular installment amount on file are left as they are. Afterwards a lookup of the arrangement shows it active, dated today, with the new balance remaining.

**How it is invoked.** This is an agent-side tool. The agent unlocks it with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool` and then calls it with `call_agent_discoverable_tool`, naming `reinstate_arrangement_7e9638f2`.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `arrangement_id` | The reference number of the deferred payment agreement being reinstated, as returned by the payment arrangement lookup for the customer's service account | Identifier, as shown in the lookup |
| `redeferred_amount` | The balance placed back under the arrangement at reinstatement | US dollars with 2 decimal places, a plain number such as 1234.56 with no currency sign or thousands separator; stored rounded half-up to the cent; must not be negative |

**Return.** A text receipt: "Arrangement <arrangement_id> reinstated: status active as of <YYYY-MM-DD>, balance remaining <amount> USD." The date is today's date, the new status date, and the amount is the balance now held under the arrangement, with 2 decimal places. Receiving this receipt means the reinstatement is recorded.

## Illustration (hypothetical values)

A call with `arrangement_id` ARR-0001 and `redeferred_amount` 1500.00 on a day dated 2026-03-02 returns: "Arrangement ARR-0001 reinstated: status active as of 2026-03-02, balance remaining 1500.00 USD." A lookup then shows the plan active, dated 2026-03-02, with 1500.00 remaining and its installment count and regular installment unchanged.

title: Security Deposits Held and Renegotiated Payment Arrangement Schedules — Basis Q&A
content:
# Security Deposits Held and Renegotiated Payment Arrangement Schedules — Basis Q&A

**Rule.** When the installment schedule of an active Payment Arrangement plan is renegotiated, the deposit months are 2 when a Security Deposit in held status on the service agreement holds at least $300.00, 1 when a held deposit holds more than zero but less than $300.00, and zero when no deposit is held on the agreement.

## Questions the rule answers

**Which deposit is read?**
The Security Deposit recorded on the same service agreement as the plan, in held status, and the amount it holds.

**What applies when the held deposit holds exactly $300.00?**
2 months — at least $300.00.

**What applies when it holds $299.99?**
1 month — more than zero and less than $300.00.

**What applies when the deposit on the agreement has been assessed but is not yet held, or has been refunded?**
Zero — no deposit is held on the agreement.

| Held deposit amount (hypothetical) | None held | $75.00 | $299.99 | $300.00 | $640.00 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Deposit months | 0 | 1 | 1 | 2 | 2 |

title: Payment Arrangement Down Payment Receipt, Activation and Lapse Standard
content:
# Payment Arrangement Down Payment Receipt, Activation and Lapse Standard

**Standard.** A Payment Arrangement plan with no down payment — zero or waived — is activated on its enrollment date. A plan with a down payment is activated when the payments posted to the service agreement on or after the enrollment date reach the down payment amount; payments from an energy assistance agency count only where the kind lets an agency payment count toward the down payment. Activation requires the down payment to be received no later than the down payment due date. A plan whose down payment is not received in time lapses on the day after the due date, and its balance never leaves the service agreement.

## The down payment due date

The due date is the enrollment date plus the kind's days to pay, in calendar days; the test is made against the due date recorded on the plan itself, with an offset of 0 days. A payment posted on the due date itself is in time.

| Hypothetical plan | Enrolled | Days to pay | Due date | Down payment completed on | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Standard Deferred Payment Agreement | June 10 | 5 | June 15 | June 15 | Activated June 15 — the due date itself is in time |
| Standard Deferred Payment Agreement | June 10 | 5 | June 15 | June 16 | Lapses on June 16, the day after the due date |
| Short-Term Installment Plan | June 10 | 3 | June 13 | $60.00 on June 11 and $40.00 on June 12 against $100.00 | Activated June 12, when posted payments reach the amount |
| Commercial Deferred Payment Agreement | June 10 | 3 | June 13 | An energy assistance agency payment on June 12 | The agency payment does not count for this kind |

## Deferral of the arrears

When a plan becomes active, the arrears are deferred into the plan: the past-due charges are moved off the service agreement's collectible balance into the plan as its deferral at activation. A deferral is booked only on a plan in active status, as the plan record shows.

## Retired clause

The former clause that on activation, and again on reinstatement, the deferred amount (or on reinstatement the remaining unbilled plan balance) is booked into the plan and credited off the service agreement's collectible balance is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis. Under the current basis, on activation the deferred amount is booked into the plan and credited off the service agreement's collectible balance. For a reinstated deferred payment agreement, the amount booked back into the plan and credited off the collectible balance is the reinstatement re-deferral, and for a reinstated Winter Protection Plan it is the winter re-deferral, in each case not the remaining unbilled plan balance.

title: Payment Arrangement Down Payment Terms by Arrangement Kind
content:
# Payment Arrangement Down Payment Terms by Arrangement Kind

A Payment Arrangement may require a down payment before it takes effect. The terms below fix, for each kind, the share of the eligible balance taken as a down payment, the share that applies instead when the agreement is disconnected at enrollment, the smallest down payment, the days allowed to pay it, and two treatments: whether a current income qualification waives it and whether a payment from an energy assistance agency counts toward it.

| Arrangement kind | Down payment share, connected agreement | Down payment share, agreement disconnected at enrollment | Minimum down payment | Days after enrollment to pay | Waived for a current income qualification | Energy assistance agency payment counts toward it |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Payment Extension | 0% | 0% | $0.00 | 0 | No | Yes |
| Short-Term Installment Plan | 30% | 50% | $50.00 | 3 | Yes | Yes |
| Standard Deferred Payment Agreement | 20% | 40% | $50.00 | 5 | Yes | Yes |
| Extended Deferred Payment Agreement | 10% | 25% | $25.00 | 7 | Yes | Yes |
| Winter Protection Plan | 0% | 0% | $0.00 | 0 | Yes | Yes |
| Arrearage Management Program | 0% | 0% | $0.00 | 0 | Yes | Yes |
| Commercial Deferred Payment Agreement | 33% | 50% | $250.00 | 3 | No | No |

## Meaning of the columns

1. **Down payment share, connected agreement** — the down payment as a fraction of the eligible balance where the agreement is not disconnected at enrollment.
2. **Down payment share, disconnected agreement** — the fraction that replaces the connected-agreement share when the agreement is disconnected at enrollment.
3. **Minimum down payment** — the smallest down payment when a down payment applies; it is never more than the eligible balance.
4. **Days to pay** — calendar days after enrollment by which the down payment must be received; 0 means the kind has no down payment phase.
5. **Income qualification waiver** — whether the down payment is waived when the customer's income qualification is current at enrollment.
6. **Agency payments** — whether a payment from an energy assistance agency counts toward the down payment.

## Points of judgement

- The Payment Extension, the Winter Protection Plan and the Arrearage Management Program carry a 0% share and 0 days to pay: they have no down payment phase.
- The Commercial Deferred Payment Agreement is the only kind for which neither the income qualification waiver nor an energy assistance agency payment applies.

title: Training Note: Early Payoff and Moving Payment Arrangement Plans Between Agreements
content:
# Training Note: Early Payoff and Moving Payment Arrangement Plans Between Agreements

Two plan features vary by kind of Payment Arrangement: whether the customer may pay the remaining plan balance at any time to complete the plan, and whether the plan moves with the customer to a new service agreement when the current one closes.

| Arrangement kind | Early payoff at any time | Plan moves to the customer's new service agreement |
|---|---|---|
| Payment Extension | Yes | No |
| Short-Term Installment Plan | Yes | Yes |
| Standard Deferred Payment Agreement | Yes | Yes |
| Extended Deferred Payment Agreement | Yes | Yes |
| Winter Protection Plan | Yes | Yes |
| Arrearage Management Program | Yes | No |
| Commercial Deferred Payment Agreement | Yes | No |

## Questions this note answers

**Can a customer on any kind of plan pay it off early?**
Yes. Every kind allows the customer to pay the remaining plan balance at any time to complete the plan.

**Which kinds can follow the customer to a new address?**
The Short-Term Installment Plan, the Standard Deferred Payment Agreement, the Extended Deferred Payment Agreement and the Winter Protection Plan. The Payment Extension, the Arrearage Management Program and the Commercial Deferred Payment Agreement do not move with the customer.

title: Arrearage Management Program — Energy Assistance Pledge Window
content:
# Arrearage Management Program — Energy Assistance Pledge Window

**Rule.** For a program bill of an Arrearage Management Program plan, the forgiveness kind of Payment Arrangement, an energy assistance agency's pledge on the agreement is on record when an earlier payment from an energy assistance agency was posted to the Electric Service Agreement within the agency pledge window before booking. The agency pledge window is:

- **12 months** when the plan carries no earlier missed-installment entry and the Electric Service Agreement's start date lies at least 120 whole calendar months before booking;
- **6 months** when exactly one of those two holds;
- **zero months**, so that no booking-day agency payment is recognised, when neither holds.

A window of a number of months before booking covers payments dated after the same calendar day that many months earlier, up to and including the booking date. Months between the start date and the booking day are counted in whole calendar months.

## Truth table

| No earlier missed-installment entry on the plan | Start date at least 120 whole calendar months before booking | Agency pledge window |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | 12 months |
| Yes | No | 6 months |
| No | Yes | 6 months |
| No | No | 0 months |

## Hypothetical reading

An agreement in service since 2012 carries a program plan with one earlier missed-installment entry; an agency paid on the agreement 4 months before booking. Exactly one condition holds, so the window is 6 months, and the payment 4 months back lies inside it.

title: Payment Arrangement Enrollment Eligibility Standards
content:
# Payment Arrangement Enrollment Eligibility Standards

The standards below decide whether a Payment Arrangement of a given kind may be enrolled on a service agreement. Each is read from the company's records on the enrollment date unless the standard itself names the customer's own statement.

## Standards in force

1. **Whose agreement.** A plan is offered only on a service agreement held by the caller's customer profile, and the kind must match the profile's customer type under that kind's entry requirements.
2. **Agreement status.** The service agreement must be in active, notice pending or disconnected status; a closed or pending start agreement cannot take a plan. The status is read from the service agreement record for the agreement the plan is for, before the plan is set up.
3. **Disconnected agreements.** A kind that is not available after disconnection is not enrolled on a disconnected agreement.
4. **Arrears age.** The oldest unpaid bill must be at least the kind's minimum arrears age past its due date.
5. **Length of service.** The service agreement's start date must be at least the kind's minimum service months before the enrollment date.
6. **Season.** The enrollment date must fall inside the kind's enrollment window.
7. **Income qualification.** An income qualification is current when the customer's income-qualified-until date is on or after the enrollment date.
8. **Extended Deferred Payment Agreement.** Requires a current income qualification or a medical certification on the agreement in active status, and an active budget billing plan on the same agreement.
9. **Winter Protection Plan.** Requires electric space heating and either a current income qualification or an account holder aged at least the kind's senior minimum age on the enrollment date.
10. **Arrearage Management Program.** Requires a current income qualification.
11. **Default lockout.** After a default on any of the customer's plans, only a Payment Extension may be enrolled until the default lockout has passed (see the counting rule below).
12. **Frequency.** The number of plans of the same kind enrolled on the agreement in the past 12 months — the 12 calendar months ending on the handling date, plans in any status — must be below the kind's enrollment limit. A customer who completed an Arrearage Management Program plan may not enroll in it again within the program's completion wait of that completion, measured from the latest completion of that kind anywhere in the customer's history.
13. **Installment count.** The customer chooses the installment count between the kind's fewest and most installments, or up to the kind's most installments after disconnection when the agreement is disconnected at enrollment. The count rests on the customer's own statement of choice for the agreement concerned.
14. **Approval limit.** A deferred amount above the kind's care-desk approval limit cannot be approved by a customer care agent and is handed to a human representative as not covered by policy.
15. **Acceptance.** The arrangement is a commitment of the customer, so it is created only on the customer's own acceptance of the stated terms.

## Retired standard

The former standard that the eligible balance, measured on the kind's balance basis, must lie between the kind's smallest and largest eligible balance is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis. Under the current basis, for every plan other than a Payment Extension on a residential agreement whose status is disconnection notice pending, the eligible balance, measured on the kind's balance basis, must lie between the kind's smallest and largest eligible balance.

## Counting the default lockout

The lockout is counted in calendar months from the posting date of the most recent default — the latest balance return for default on any of the customer's plans, on any service agreement — and it has passed on the same day of the month the lockout months later or, if that month is shorter, on its last day. The lockout has passed on that day itself: an enrollment dated on that day or later is outside the lockout, and one dated the day before is inside it.

| Most recent default posted (hypothetical) | Lockout months | Lockout has passed on | Enrollment on | Kinds other than a Payment Extension |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| March 15 | 12 | March 15 of the next year | March 14 of the next year | Not yet |
| March 15 | 12 | March 15 of the next year | March 15 of the next year | No longer locked out |
| February 29 | 12 | February 28 of the next year (shorter month, last day) | February 28 of the next year | No longer locked out |

title: Payment Arrangement Quick Reference — Enrollment Frequency, Default Lockout and Open Plans
content:
# Payment Arrangement Quick Reference — Enrollment Frequency, Default Lockout and Open Plans

How often each kind of Payment Arrangement may be taken, how long a default keeps the customer out of the installment kinds, the re-enrollment wait after completing a plan, and how many plans may be open at once on one service agreement.

| Arrangement kind | Enrollments of this kind on the same agreement within any rolling 12 months | Default lockout (months) | Wait after completing this kind before enrolling in it again (months) | Plans open at once on one agreement |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Payment Extension | 2 | 6 | 0 (none) | 1 |
| Short-Term Installment Plan | 1 | 12 | 0 (none) | 1 |
| Standard Deferred Payment Agreement | 1 | 12 | 0 (none) | 1 |
| Extended Deferred Payment Agreement | 1 | 12 | 0 (none) | 1 |
| Winter Protection Plan | 1 | 12 | 0 (none) | 1 |
| Arrearage Management Program | 1 | 12 | 12 | 1 |
| Commercial Deferred Payment Agreement | 1 | 12 | 0 (none) | 1 |

## Terms used in the card

- **Enrollments within 12 months**: plans of the same kind on the same service agreement whose enrolled date falls within the 12 calendar months ending on the handling date, counted in any status — pending down payment, active, completed, defaulted or cancelled. A new plan of the kind is possible only while that count is below the figure in the table.
- **Default lockout**: the months after a default during which no plan other than a Payment Extension may be enrolled for the customer.
- **Open plan**: a plan in pending down payment, active or defaulted status.
- **Completion wait**: months after completing the plan before the customer may enroll in the same kind again; 0 means there is no wait.

## Hypothetical illustrations

| Situation (hypothetical) | Reading of the card |
|---|---|
| Two Payment Extensions enrolled on the agreement 3 and 7 months ago, one completed and one cancelled | Count is 2, equal to the figure of 2; no third Payment Extension on that agreement yet |
| One Short-Term Installment Plan enrolled 11 months ago and completed | Count is 1, equal to the figure of 1; no second one yet |
| Arrearage Management Program completed 8 months ago | Inside the 12-month completion wait for that program |

title: Arrearage Management Program Fact Sheet — Forgiveness Terms Across Payment Arrangement Kinds
content:
# Arrearage Management Program Fact Sheet — Forgiveness Terms Across Payment Arrangement Kinds

Of the seven kinds of Payment Arrangement, only the Arrearage Management Program forgives arrears; every other kind is a repayment plan. The forgiveness terms of each kind are:

| Arrangement kind | Share of each scheduled installment forgiven when the current bill is paid in full by its due date | When forgiveness is posted | Lifetime ceiling on arrears forgiven per customer | Withheld forgiveness restored once the late bill is paid in full |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Payment Extension | 0% | Not applicable | $0.00 | No |
| Short-Term Installment Plan | 0% | Not applicable | $0.00 | No |
| Standard Deferred Payment Agreement | 0% | Not applicable | $0.00 | No |
| Extended Deferred Payment Agreement | 0% | Not applicable | $0.00 | No |
| Winter Protection Plan | 0% | Not applicable | $0.00 | No |
| Arrearage Management Program | 100% | Posted on the day after the due date of the bill whose current charges were paid in full by that due date | $8000.00 | Yes |
| Commercial Deferred Payment Agreement | 0% | Not applicable | $0.00 | No |

## About the program terms

- **Share forgiven**: the fraction of each scheduled installment forgiven, instead of billed, when the current bill is paid in full by its due date. In the Arrearage Management Program the share is 100%, the whole scheduled installment.
- **Lifetime ceiling**: the ceiling applies to the arrears forgiven across all of a customer's Arrearage Management Program plans, not to one plan.
- **Restoring withheld forgiveness**: in the Arrearage Management Program, forgiveness withheld for a late current bill can be restored once that bill is paid in full.

## Example (hypothetical dates)

A program bill dated March 4 falls due on March 25 and its current charges are paid in full on March 22. Under the posting term in the table, the forgiveness for the installment that bill carries is posted on March 26, the day after the due date.

title: Payment Arrangement Hardship Treatment of the Restoration Share
content:
# Payment Arrangement Hardship Treatment of the Restoration Share

**Rule.** When a defaulted Standard Deferred Payment Agreement or Extended Deferred Payment Agreement of the Payment Arrangement program is reinstated, the hardship treatment applies when the service agreement carries an active medical protection under the Medical and Life-Support Protections or an active Budget Billing plan:

1. When the agreement carries **both**, the missed-installment share is left out of the combined restoration share before that share is floored at zero; the result is the restoration share.
2. When it carries **exactly one** of the two, the combined restoration share, floored at zero, is halved; the result is the restoration share.
3. When it carries **neither**, the combined restoration share, floored at zero, is used as it stands.

The records read are the status of the medical protection and of the budget billing plan held on the same service agreement; only an active one counts.

## Truth table

| Active medical protection on the agreement | Active Budget Billing plan on the agreement | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | Missed-installment share left out, then floored at zero |
| Yes | No | Floored at zero, then halved |
| No | Yes | Floored at zero, then halved |
| No | No | Floored at zero, used as it stands |

## Worked cases (hypothetical shares)

| Combined restoration share | Of which the missed-installment share | Holdings | Restoration share |
|---|---|---|---|
| 21% | 15% | Both | 21% less 15%: 6% |
| 21% | 15% | Medical protection only | 21% halved: 10.5% |
| 21% | 15% | Neither | 21% |
| 6% | 10% | Both | 6% less 10% is below zero: 0 |
| Below zero | 0 | Budget Billing only | Floored at zero, halved: 0 |

title: Payment Arrangement Installments on the Regular Electric Bill
content:
# Payment Arrangement Installments on the Regular Electric Bill

**Rule.** Installments of a Payment Arrangement are billed one per regular bill of the service agreement, starting with the bill the kind names for the first installment, numbered from 1 in billing order, and the numbering continues after a reinstatement or a renegotiation. Each installment number is billed once. An installment is billed only while the plan is active. The billed installment is the regular installment amount, except the last, which carries the remainder of the plan balance, and it falls due on the due date of the bill that carries it. Installments of an Arrearage Management Program plan are billed only when forgiveness is withheld or the forgiveness room is exhausted. Early payoff is made by the customer paying the remaining plan balance; it is booked as a return of the balance for early payoff and completes the plan.

## What a billed installment does

Billing an installment takes it out of the plan balance and places it on the service agreement's bill as an arrangement installment charge, dated with the bill date of the bill carrying it.

## Conditions at a glance

| Question | Answer under the rule |
|---|---|
| May installment 3 be billed twice? | No — each installment number is billed once, and a number already forgiven is not billed either |
| May an installment be billed while the plan is defaulted or pending its down payment? | No — only while the plan is active |
| Which installment carries the rounding remainder? | The last one |
| When does an installment fall due? | On the due date of the bill carrying it |
| Does the numbering restart after a reinstatement? | No — it continues |

## Hypothetical schedule

A plan with a deferred amount of $500.00 over 3 installments has a regular installment of $166.66. Installments 1 and 2 bill $166.66 each on the first two regular bills after activation; installment 3, the last, carries the remainder of the plan balance, $166.68.

title: Payment Arrangement Renegotiation of the Installment Count
content:
# Payment Arrangement Renegotiation of the Installment Count

## Clauses in force

1. An active Payment Arrangement plan may have its installment count changed only where the kind allows renegotiation (its renegotiations allowed is above zero) and the plan has not been renegotiated before.
2. Renegotiation is made only on a plan in active status with no installment currently counted as missed, as the plan record shows.
3. Renegotiation never changes the deferred amount or re-ages any missed installment.

A renegotiation records the new total installment count, counting the installments already billed, and the new regular installment for the installments not yet billed.

## Retired clauses

- The former clause that the new total installment count, counting installments already billed, may not exceed the kind's renegotiation ceiling, and that the regular installment for the installments not yet billed is the unbilled plan balance divided by the number of installments remaining, rounded down to the cent, with the final installment carrying the remainder, is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis.
- The former clause that the new count is chosen by the customer is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis.

## Points of judgement (hypothetical plans)

| Plan | Status | Installment counted as missed | Renegotiated before | Kind allows renegotiation | May be renegotiated |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Standard Deferred Payment Agreement | Active | None | No | Yes | Yes |
| Extended Deferred Payment Agreement | Active | One | No | Yes | No |
| Standard Deferred Payment Agreement | Active | None | Yes | Yes | No |
| Short-Term Installment Plan | Active | None | No | No | No |

title: Customer Action Card — Payment Arrangement Installment Schedule Renegotiation
content:
# Customer Action Card — Payment Arrangement Installment Schedule Renegotiation

**Terms.** A customer may ask to change the installment schedule of a Payment Arrangement plan after a change in circumstances. A renegotiation follows the renegotiation rule of the Payment Arrangement program except where these terms set the schedule. Renegotiation is made only on a plan in active status with no installment currently counted as missed, and a plan is renegotiated no more than the number of times its kind allows. The renegotiation is made only on the customer's own acceptance of that schedule.

## Defaulted plans

Where the plan has defaulted, its new regular installment is worked out only after the plan stands in active status again with its reinstatement re-deferral booked back under it as its remaining balance.

## The customer's acceptance — `renegotiate_arrangement_installments_743d0532`

**What the tool records.** The customer's own acceptance of a new installment schedule on one of their payment arrangements. The customer, acting in person, confirms a new total number of installments for the arrangement identified by the reference number (the total counts the installments already billed) and the new regular installment that will be billed for each installment not yet billed; the final installment carries whatever remainder is left. The arrangement's installment count and regular installment amount are replaced by the values confirmed; its status, balance and deferred amount are unchanged. Afterwards a lookup of the arrangement shows the new count and amount.

**How it is invoked.** This is a customer's own tool. The agent unlocks it with `unlock_user_discoverable_tool` and hands it over; the customer themselves then runs it with `call_user_discoverable_tool`, naming `renegotiate_arrangement_installments_743d0532`.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `arrangement_id` | The reference number of the customer's payment arrangement whose schedule is being changed, as the representative reads it out from the payment arrangement lookup | Identifier, as shown in the lookup |
| `installment_count` | The new total number of installments of the arrangement, counting those already billed | Whole number (integer), at least 1 |
| `installment_amount` | The new regular installment for each installment not yet billed | US dollars with 2 decimal places, a plain number such as 87.63 with no currency sign; stored rounded half-up to the cent |

**Return.** A text receipt: "Arrangement <arrangement_id> schedule changed: <count> installments in total, regular installment <amount> USD." The count is the new total as an integer and the amount the new regular installment with 2 decimal places. Receiving this receipt means the new schedule is recorded.

## Illustration (hypothetical values)

The customer runs the tool with `arrangement_id` ARR-0002, `installment_count` 9 and `installment_amount` 242.48. The receipt reads: "Arrangement ARR-0002 schedule changed: 9 installments in total, regular installment 242.48 USD." The plan's status and the balance held under it are as they were before.

title: Payment Arrangement Installment Schedule Terms
content:
# Payment Arrangement Installment Schedule Terms

These terms fix, for each kind of Payment Arrangement, the installment counts the customer may choose, the smallest installment, which bill carries the first installment, when each installment falls due, how the deferred amount is split, and the longest date extension a Payment Extension may give.

## Installment counts and minimum installment

| Arrangement kind | Fewest installments | Most installments, connected agreement | Most installments, agreement disconnected at enrollment | Smallest installment |

| Payment Extension | 1 | 1 | 1 | $0.00 |
| Short-Term Installment Plan | 2 | 3 | 2 | $25.00 |
| Standard Deferred Payment Agreement | 4 | 6 | 4 | $25.00 |
| Extended Deferred Payment Agreement | 7 | 12 | 9 | $25.00 |
| Winter Protection Plan | 8 | 8 | 8 | $10.00 |
| Arrearage Management Program | 12 | 12 | 12 | $0.00 |
| Commercial Deferred Payment Agreement | 2 | 4 | 3 | $100.00 |

## Billing and splitting of installments

| Arrangement kind | First installment carried by | Each installment falls due | Splitting of the deferred amount | Longest extension of the due date |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Payment Extension | A single installment billed on the extended due date | On the extended due date | A single installment equal to the deferred amount | 14 calendar days |
| Short-Term Installment Plan | First regular bill issued after activation | On the due date of the bill carrying it | Equal installments rounded down to the cent; the final installment carries the remainder | 0 |
| Standard Deferred Payment Agreement | First regular bill issued after activation | On the due date of the bill carrying it | Equal installments rounded down to the cent; the final installment carries the remainder | 0 |
| Extended Deferred Payment Agreement | First regular bill issued after activation | On the due date of the bill carrying it | Equal installments rounded down to the cent; the final installment carries the remainder | 0 |
| Winter Protection Plan | First regular bill dated after 03-31 following enrollment | On the due date of the bill carrying it | Equal installments rounded down to the cent; the final installment carries the remainder | 0 |
| Arrearage Management Program | First regular bill issued after activation | Scheduled with the bill carrying it; forgiven instead of billed when that bill is paid in full by its due date | Equal installments rounded down to the cent; the final installment carries the remainder | 0 |
| Commercial Deferred Payment Agreement | First regular bill issued after activation | On the due date of the bill carrying it | Equal installments rounded down to the cent; the final installment carries the remainder | 0 |

## Notes

- The smallest installment is the floor against which the chosen count is reduced: the installment count is reduced until each installment reaches it.
- The longest extension applies to the Payment Extension only; the installment kinds carry 0 days.

| Deferred amount | Count | Regular installment (rounded down to the cent) | Final installment (carries the remainder) |
