title: Payment Arrangement Installments Counted as Used on Renegotiation
content:
# Payment Arrangement Installments Counted as Used on Renegotiation

**Rule.** When the installment schedule of an active Payment Arrangement plan is renegotiated, the installments counted as used are:

1. the installments billed on the plan less every installment recorded as missed on it, when a payment from an energy assistance agency was posted to the Electric Service Agreement within the 12 months before the renegotiation;
2. the installments billed less one installment recorded as missed (none when the plan carries no missed-installment entry), when no such agency payment was posted but an autopay payment was posted within the 3 months before the renegotiation;
3. all the installments billed, in every other case.

The payments read are those on the Electric Service Agreement's payment records whose channel is an energy assistance agency or autopay; the installments read are the plan's installment billings and its missed-installment entries. A window of a number of months before the renegotiation covers payments posted after the same calendar day that many months earlier, up to and including the renegotiation date.

## Input — judgement — output (hypothetical plan: 5 installments billed, 2 recorded as missed)

| Agency payment within 12 months | Autopay payment within 3 months | Judgement | Installments counted as used |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | Either | First case | 5 less 2: 3 |
| No | Yes | Second case | 5 less 1: 4 |
| No | No | Third case | 5 |

## Same tests on a plan with no missed-installment entry (5 billed)

| Agency payment within 12 months | Autopay payment within 3 months | Installments counted as used |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Either | 5 |
| No | Yes | 5 — no missed entry to take away |
| No | No | 5 |

title: Payment Arrangement Coordination With Budget Billing, Deposits, Disconnection and Late Charges
content:
# Payment Arrangement Coordination With Budget Billing, Deposits, Disconnection and Late Charges

**Rules.**

1. **Budget Billing.** Holding an active budget billing plan on the same service agreement is required for the Extended Deferred Payment Agreement and does not change any other Payment Arrangement kind's terms.
2. **Disconnection.** An active arrangement on a service agreement suspends disconnection for nonpayment of the deferred balance while installments and current bills are paid as agreed.
3. **Winter and forgiveness plans.** A Winter Protection Plan and an Arrearage Management Program plan exclude each other on the same agreement through the one-open-plan rule; a customer in the winter enrollment window who qualifies for both chooses one.
4. **Security Deposit.** A security deposit held on the agreement is never applied to plan installments while the plan is active.
5. **Late payment charges.** Installments, returned plan balances and program debits never attract a late payment charge on the service agreement.

## Questions the rules answer

**Does an active budget billing plan change the down payment or installment count of a Standard Deferred Payment Agreement?** No. Budget billing is a requirement of the Extended Deferred Payment Agreement and changes no other kind's terms.

**May a held deposit be used to pay an installment that is coming due?** Not while the plan is active.

**Is a late payment charge assessed on a returned plan balance after a default?** No. Returned plan balances never attract a late payment charge.

**Can a customer hold both a Winter Protection Plan and an Arrearage Management Program plan on one agreement?** No; only one plan is open on an agreement, and a customer qualifying for both chooses one.

title: Late Payment Charges and Arrearage Management Program Catch-Up Forgiveness — Basis Q&A
content:
# Late Payment Charges and Arrearage Management Program Catch-Up Forgiveness — Basis Q&A

**Rule.** When withheld forgiveness on a program bill of an Arrearage Management Program plan, the forgiveness kind of Payment Arrangement, is posted as a catch-up, the late-charge cut is 15% when 3 or more late payment charges were posted to the Electric Service Agreement within the 6 months before the posting, 5% when at least one but fewer than 3 were, and zero when none was. A window of 6 months before the posting covers charges posted after the same calendar day 6 months earlier, up to and including the posting date.

## Questions the rule answers

**Which charges are counted?**
Late payment charges on the Electric Service Agreement's ledger, posted within the 6 months before the posting.

**What applies with exactly 3 late payment charges?** 15%.

**What applies with 2?** 5%.

**What applies with 1?** 5%.

**What applies with none?** Zero.

**Does a late payment charge posted 6 months and 1 day before the posting count?** No — it lies before the window.

| Late payment charges in the 6 months | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Late-charge cut | 0 | 5% | 5% | 15% | 15% |

title: Arrearage Management Program Lateness Cut — Decision Table
content:
# Arrearage Management Program Lateness Cut — Decision Table

**Rule.** When withheld forgiveness on a program bill of an Arrearage Management Program plan, the forgiveness kind of Payment Arrangement, is posted as a catch-up, the lateness cut is:

| Missed-installment entry on the plan | Days late of the program bill when it was paid in full | Lateness cut |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | More than 7 | 50% |
| Yes | 7 or fewer | 25% |
| No | Any | 0 |

The missed-installment entries read are those standing on the plan's history. The days late are the days between the point from which lateness is counted for the bill and the date the bill was paid in full.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical plan carrying a missed-installment entry)

| Days late | More than 7 | Lateness cut |
|---|---|---|
| 6 | No | 25% |
| 7 | No — exactly 7 is not more than 7 | 25% |
| 8 | Yes | 50% |

A plan with no missed-installment entry carries no lateness cut, however late the bill was paid in full.

title: Arrearage Management Program — Forgiveness Cap Measured per Customer
content:
# Arrearage Management Program — Forgiveness Cap Measured per Customer

**Rule.** Forgiveness under the Arrearage Management Program, the forgiveness kind of Payment Arrangement, is capped per customer, not per plan. The cap is the program's lifetime forgiveness cap per customer, and it is measured against the total of all forgiveness entries posted on all of the customer's Arrearage Management Program plans, across every service agreement the customer has held. The remaining room is the cap less the amount already forgiven.

1. **At enrollment.** The eligible balance placed under a new Arrearage Management Program plan may not exceed the remaining room. Any part of the past-due balance above that room stays on the service agreement, and it may be placed in a separate repayment plan only after the program plan ends.
2. **At each forgiveness.** A forgiveness that would carry the customer's total past the cap is reduced to the remaining room.
3. **Once the room is zero.** The remaining scheduled installments are billed as ordinary installments instead of being forgiven.

## Worked figures (hypothetical customer, program cap $8000.00)

| Step | Figure |
|---|---|
| Forgiven to date on two earlier program plans | $6500.00 |
| Remaining room | $8000.00 less $6500.00, that is $1500.00 |
| Past-due balance offered for a new program plan | $2300.00 |
| Balance placed under the new program plan | $1500.00 |
| Part left on the service agreement | $800.00, available for a separate repayment plan only after the program plan ends |

Later on the same plan, with $120.00 of room left, a scheduled installment of $200.00 is earned for forgiveness: $120.00 is forgiven, the room becomes zero, and every scheduled installment after it is billed as an ordinary installment.

## Basis Q&A

**Does the cap reset for a new service agreement or a new plan?** No. The measure runs over the customer's whole history across all service agreements.

**Does the cap apply to the repayment kinds?** The repayment kinds never forgive; the cap concerns Arrearage Management Program forgiveness.

title: Arrearage Management Program Missed Program-Bill Amount — Calculation Memo
content:
# Arrearage Management Program Missed Program-Bill Amount — Calculation Memo

This memorandum sets the amount recorded when a program bill of an Arrearage Management Program plan, the forgiveness kind of Payment Arrangement, is booked as missed. The booking day is the day after the cure period ends.

## 1. The bill and the payments that count

The program bill is the agreement's most recent bill, by bill date. For a program bill, payments applied oldest charges first by the end of the cure period count toward its program obligation, and a payment posted on the booking day counts toward it only where this calculation recognises it.

## 2. The program obligation

As standard, the program obligation of the bill is the bill's current charges. As standard, a re-base reads the agreement's bills over the 6 months before booking.

## 3. The unpaid program obligation

The unpaid program obligation is the smaller of:

1. the program obligation, and
2. the agreement's balance at the end of the cure period less the agreement's latest late payment charge, where that charge was posted after the bill date.

The agreement's balance at the end of the cure period is its balance at booking plus every payment posted to it on the booking day, an energy assistance agency's included.

## 4. The recognised booking-day payments

The recognised booking-day payments are the recognised customer booking-day payments plus the recognised agency booking-day payment. As standard, no payment posted on the booking day is recognised. The recognised agency booking-day payment is the payment an energy assistance agency posted to the agreement on the booking day when the agency's pledge on the agreement is on record, that is when an earlier payment from an energy assistance agency was posted to the agreement within the agency pledge window before booking, the booking-day payment itself left out; it is zero otherwise.

## 5. The missed program-bill amount

The missed program-bill amount is the unpaid program obligation less the recognised booking-day payments, rounded half-up to the cent and never below zero.

A window of a number of months before booking covers entries dated after the same calendar day that many months earlier, up to and including the booking date.

## Worked examples (hypothetical program bill dated March 3, current charges $184.20, booking day April 8)

| Line | Case 1 | Case 2 |
|---|---|---|
| Balance at booking | $260.55 | $95.30 |
| Payments posted on the booking day, of every channel | $40.00 by card | None |
| Balance at the end of the cure period | $300.55 | $95.30 |
| Latest late payment charge, posted after March 3 | $9.50 on March 28 | $6.10 on March 28 |
| Balance less that charge | $291.05 | $89.20 |
| Program obligation | $184.20 | $184.20 |
| Unpaid program obligation (the smaller) | $184.20 | $89.20 |
| Recognised booking-day payments | $0.00 | $0.00 |
| Missed program-bill amount | $184.20 | $89.20 |

A late payment charge posted on or before the bill date is not taken off the balance.

title: Arrearage Management Program — Missed Program Bill Entries
content:
# Arrearage Management Program — Missed Program Bill Entries

**Rule.** A program bill of an Arrearage Management Program plan — the forgiveness kind of Payment Arrangement — whose current charges are still unpaid when its cure period ends is booked as a missed-installment entry for the installment that bill carries, on the day after the cure period ends. The amount the entry records is the missed program-bill amount. The rules of the Payment Arrangement program on cure periods, on counting missed installments and on default are unchanged: the entry counts toward the plan's missed installments like any other missed installment.

## Booking the entry — `record_missed_program_bill_7606bb4e`

**What the tool does.** It records that a program bill of an Arrearage Management Program plan is counted as missed. A missed-installment entry dated today is added to the plan's history for the installment number that bill carries, linked to the bill and carrying the missed amount given. The plan's status and balance are not changed. Afterwards the plan history shows the missed entry.

**How it is invoked.** This is an agent-side tool. The agent unlocks it with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool` and then calls it with `call_agent_discoverable_tool`, naming `record_missed_program_bill_7606bb4e`.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `arrangement_id` | The reference number of the Arrearage Management Program plan, as returned by the payment arrangement lookup | Identifier |
| `installment_number` | The position of the scheduled installment the missed bill carries (1 is the first) | Whole number (integer) |
| `bill_id` | The bill reference number of the program bill counted as missed, as returned by the bill lookup | Identifier |
| `amount` | The missed amount recorded | US dollars with 2 decimal places, a plain number such as 11.91 with no currency sign; stored rounded half-up to the cent |

**Return.** A text receipt: "Missed entry <entry_id> recorded on <arrangement_id> for installment <n>: <amount> USD." The entry identifier is the reference number of the new history entry, the installment number is the one given and the amount carries 2 decimal places. Receiving this receipt means the entry is recorded.

## Timing at a glance (hypothetical program bill)

| Due date | Cure period | Last cure day | Current charges paid in full by the last cure day | Missed-installment entry |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| May 20 | 10 days | May 30 | Yes | None |
| May 20 | 10 days | May 30 | No | Booked on May 31 for the installment the bill carries |

title: Payment Arrangement Holdings Across a Customer's Service Agreements
content:
# Payment Arrangement Holdings Across a Customer's Service Agreements

**Clause.** A customer may hold Payment Arrangement plans on several service agreements at the same time, one per service agreement. A plan is enrolled on a service agreement only when no other plan on that same agreement is in pending down payment, active or defaulted status, as the company's arrangement records for that agreement show before the plan is set up. A defaulted plan that is still inside its reinstatement window therefore blocks a new plan on that agreement until the window ends or the plan is reinstated. Plans on different service agreements of the same customer are decided independently, except where a rule of the Payment Arrangement program counts the customer's whole history — defaults and Arrearage Management Program forgiveness. No ceiling is set on the number of service agreements on which one customer holds a plan.

## Status of another plan on the same agreement

| Status of the other plan on the same service agreement | Blocks a new plan on that agreement |
|---|---|
| Pending down payment | Yes |
| Active | Yes |
| Defaulted, reinstatement window still open | Yes |
| Defaulted, reinstatement window ended | Yes — a defaulted plan is still in defaulted status |
| Completed | No |
| Cancelled | No |

The record that decides the question is the arrangement record of the agreement the new plan is for: a plan held on another of the customer's agreements does not count against this one.

## Hypothetical cases

1. A customer holds an active Standard Deferred Payment Agreement on the agreement for a home and asks for a Short-Term Installment Plan on the agreement for a rental property with no plan on it. The second agreement carries no open plan, so the rule in this clause does not stand in the way.
2. The same customer asks for a Payment Extension on the home agreement while the Standard Deferred Payment Agreement is active there. The active plan is an open plan on that agreement, so no second plan is enrolled on it.
3. A plan on an agreement was completed last month. A completed plan is not an open plan.

title: Payment Extension on an Agreement Under Disconnection Notice — Calculation Memo
content:
# Payment Extension on an Agreement Under Disconnection Notice — Calculation Memo

This memorandum sets the balance placed under a Payment Extension, the part due now and the amount carried to the extended date, for a Payment Extension — the single-installment kind of Payment Arrangement — enrolled on the customer's residential service agreement whose status is disconnection notice pending.

## 1. The extension base

The balance placed under a payment extension is the extension base. As standard, the extension base is the agreement's past-due balance on the enrollment date: its bills whose due date falls on or before the enrollment date plus its posted charges, less its payments and credits, all read over the 240 months before the enrollment date, the total rounded to the cent.

## 2. The part due now and the amount carried

- The **part due now** is the extension base times the upfront share, rounded half-up to the cent.
- The **amount carried** by the extension is the extension base less the part due now, rounded half-up to the cent.

## 3. The upfront share

The upfront share is the default share plus the returned-payment share, less the forgiveness relief, less the tenure relief and less the assistance relief; these are first added together into one share, applied once to the extension base, and a combined share below zero counts as zero. The standard upfront share is zero, so that the whole extension base is carried to the extended date.

A window of a number of months before enrollment covers entries dated after the same calendar day that many months earlier, up to and including the enrollment date.

## Worked memo (hypothetical agreement, enrollment dated April 14)

| Line | Figure |
|---|---|
| Bills due on or before April 14, within the 240 months | $4812.40 |
| Posted charges in the same period | $96.25 |
| Payments and credits in the same period | $4410.00 |
| Past-due balance: $4812.40 plus $96.25 less $4410.00 | $498.65 |
| Extension base | $498.65 |
| Upfront share | 0 |
| Part due now | $0.00 |
| Amount carried to the extended date | $498.65 |

title: Payment Extension Terms on Residential Agreements Under Disconnection Notice — Customer Action Card
content:
# Payment Extension Terms on Residential Agreements Under Disconnection Notice — Customer Action Card

**Scope.** These terms set the Payment Extension — the one-time, single-installment kind of Payment Arrangement — enrolled on a residential service agreement of the customer whose status is disconnection notice pending. Extensions on other agreements follow the general Payment Arrangement terms, and the general eligibility, one-open-plan, lockout and single-installment rules are unchanged.

## Terms

1. The extension base must lie between the Payment Extension's smallest and largest eligible balance.
2. The amount carried by a payment extension is fixed only after every program bill of the customer that has been paid in full carries the forgiveness entry owed for it.
3. The amount carried by a payment extension is not worked out until every Winter Protection Plan of the customer that defaulted and has had its missed installments and good-faith payment paid inside its reinstatement window stands active again.

## The customer's acceptance — `accept_payment_extension_fc63ed0e`

**What the tool records.** The customer's own acceptance of a Payment Extension on one of their electric service agreements. The customer, acting in person, accepts a Payment Extension: the balance placed under it, the part of that balance to be paid now, and the amount carried to the extended date as one single installment. A new Payment Extension is created for the service agreement, set up by an agent, dated today, in pending down payment status with today as the last day for the payment due now, one installment equal to the amount extended, and nothing yet deferred off the agreement. A lookup of the customer's payment arrangements then shows the new extension.

**How it is invoked.** This is a customer's own tool. The agent unlocks it with `unlock_user_discoverable_tool` and hands it over; the customer themselves then runs it with `call_user_discoverable_tool`, naming `accept_payment_extension_fc63ed0e`.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `customer_id` | The customer reference number of the account holder, as returned by the customer profile lookup | Identifier |
| `service_account_id` | The service account number of the agreement the extension is for, as printed on the customer's disconnection notice and returned by the service agreement lookup | Identifier |
| `eligible_balance` | The balance placed under the extension | US dollars with 2 decimal places, a plain number such as 512.40 with no currency sign; stored rounded half-up to the cent |
| `down_payment_amount` | The part of that balance to be paid now | US dollars with 2 decimal places, 0.00 when nothing is due now; stored rounded half-up to the cent |
| `extended_amount` | The amount carried to the extended date as the single installment | US dollars with 2 decimal places; stored rounded half-up to the cent |

**Return.** A text receipt: "Payment Extension <arrangement_id> accepted on <service_account_id>: balance <eligible> USD, due now <due_now> USD by <YYYY-MM-DD>, extended <extended> USD." The reference number is that of the new arrangement, the date is today's date and the amounts carry 2 decimal places. Receiving this receipt means the extension is recorded.

## Illustration (hypothetical values)

The customer runs the tool with `customer_id` CUST-0005, `service_account_id` SA-0005, `eligible_balance` 512.40, `down_payment_amount` 0.00 and `extended_amount` 512.40 on a day dated 2026-04-14. The receipt reads: "Payment Extension <arrangement_id> accepted on SA-0005: balance 512.40 USD, due now 0.00 USD by 2026-04-14, extended 512.40 USD."

title: Payment Arrangement Payment History Cut — Decision Table for Renegotiated Schedules
content:
# Payment Arrangement Payment History Cut — Decision Table for Renegotiated Schedules

**Rule.** When the installment schedule of an active Payment Arrangement plan is renegotiated, the history cut is read from the charges posted to the Electric Service Agreement within the 12 months before the renegotiation:

| Returned-payment charge posted within the 12 months | Late payment charges posted within the 12 months | History cut |
|---|---|---|
| One or more | Any number | 2 months |
| None | 3 or more | 1 month |
| None | Fewer than 3 | 0 |

A window of 12 months before the renegotiation covers charges posted after the same calendar day 12 months earlier, up to and including the renegotiation date.

## Input — judgement — output (hypothetical agreements, renegotiation dated August 14)

| Charges on the Electric Service Agreement | Judgement | History cut |
|---|---|---|
| A returned-payment charge on December 2 of the previous year, 4 late payment charges | Returned payment inside the window | 2 months |
| A returned-payment charge on August 14 of the previous year, 3 late payment charges in the window | That charge is not after August 14 of the previous year, so outside the window; 3 late charges | 1 month |
| No returned-payment charge, 2 late payment charges | Neither condition met | 0 |

title: Payment Arrangement Payment Performance Standards — Cure Periods and Default Counts
content:
# Payment Arrangement Payment Performance Standards — Cure Periods and Default Counts

While a Payment Arrangement is in force, each kind sets the shortfall still treated as paid, whether the current bill must also be paid on time, the cure period after a due date, the extra cure days given while a medical certification is active, the number of missed installments that defaults the plan, and what becomes of the plan balance on default.

| Arrangement kind | Shortfall still treated as paid | Current bill must also be paid by its due date | Cure period (calendar days) | Extra cure days with an active medical certification | Missed installments that default the plan | Plan balance on default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Payment Extension | $0.00 | Yes | 0 | 0 | 1 | Remaining balance returned to the service agreement and due immediately |
| Short-Term Installment Plan | $1.00 | Yes | 5 | 10 | 1 | Remaining balance returned to the service agreement and due immediately |
| Standard Deferred Payment Agreement | $1.00 | Yes | 10 | 10 | 2 | Remaining balance returned to the service agreement and due immediately |
| Extended Deferred Payment Agreement | $1.00 | Yes | 10 | 15 | 2 | Remaining balance returned to the service agreement and due immediately |
| Winter Protection Plan | $1.00 | Yes | 10 | 10 | 2 | Remaining balance returned to the service agreement and due immediately |
| Arrearage Management Program | $1.00 | Yes | 10 | 10 | 2 | Unforgiven balance returned to the service agreement and due immediately |
| Commercial Deferred Payment Agreement | $0.00 | Yes | 5 | 0 | 1 | Remaining balance returned to the service agreement and due immediately |

## Definitions

- **Shortfall still treated as paid** — the amount by which a payment may fall short of an installment while the installment is still treated as paid.
- **Cure period** — the calendar days after an installment's due date within which paying it prevents it from counting as missed.
- **Extra cure days** — days added to the cure period while a medical certification on the agreement is active.
- **Missed installments that default the plan** — the number of missed installments, counted after the cure period, at which the plan defaults.

## Reading the table (hypothetical plans)

| Hypothetical plan | Cure days available after a due date |
|---|---|
| Standard Deferred Payment Agreement, no medical certification | 10 |
| Extended Deferred Payment Agreement, medical certification active | 10 and 15 more, 25 in all |
| Commercial Deferred Payment Agreement | 5; no medical extension |
| Payment Extension | 0 |

title: Payment Arrangement Plans When the Customer Moves
content:
# Payment Arrangement Plans When the Customer Moves

**Rule.** When the customer stops electric service at one address and starts service at another, an active Payment Arrangement plan of a kind that moves with the customer moves to the new service agreement. The plan moves only to a service agreement of the same customer that is pending start or active, as the service agreement record shows. The installment schedule, the installment numbering and the missed-installment count continue unchanged, and the next installment is billed on the first regular bill of the new agreement. Plans of a kind that does not move, and plans of a different customer, never move; they end with the closing agreement.

## Moving a plan — conditions and results

| Condition | Result |
|---|---|
| Kind moves with the customer; new agreement of the same customer, pending start | Plan moves |
| Kind moves with the customer; new agreement of the same customer, active | Plan moves |
| New agreement belongs to a different customer | Plan does not move |
| Kind does not move with the customer | Plan does not move |

## What carries over (hypothetical plan)

An active Winter Protection Plan has billed installments 1 to 3 of 8 and carries one missed installment. After the move, installment 4 is billed on the first regular bill of the new agreement, the remaining installments keep their numbers, and the plan still carries one missed installment.

title: Payment Arrangement Prior Default Cut on Renegotiated Schedules
content:
# Payment Arrangement Prior Default Cut on Renegotiated Schedules

**Clause.** When the installment schedule of an active Payment Arrangement plan is renegotiated, the default cut is 2 months when a balance-return entry with reason default was posted on the plan within the 6 months before the renegotiation; 1 month when such an entry was posted within the 12 months before the renegotiation but none within the 6 months; and zero when none was posted within the 12 months. A window of a number of months before the renegotiation covers entries posted after the same calendar day that many months earlier, up to and including the renegotiation date.

The entries read are the plan's own balance-return entries with reason default — the entry booked when the plan defaulted and its balance went back onto the service agreement.

## Calendar cases (hypothetical renegotiation dated October 20)

| Latest balance-return entry with reason default on the plan | Within 6 months (after April 20) | Within 12 months (after October 20 of the previous year) | Default cut |
|---|---|---|---|
| June 3 | Yes | Yes | 2 months |
| April 20 | No | Yes | 1 month |
| January 9 | No | Yes | 1 month |
| October 20 of the previous year | No | No | 0 |
| None on the plan | No | No | 0 |

title: Payment Extension Prior Default Share — Truth Table
content:
# Payment Extension Prior Default Share — Truth Table

**Rule.** For a Payment Extension — the single-installment kind of Payment Arrangement — enrolled on a residential agreement under disconnection notice, the default share is:

- **30%** when a Winter Protection Plan of the customer stands in default and 2 or more missed-installment entries were posted on the customer's plans within the 12 months before enrollment;
- **15%** when a Winter Protection Plan of the customer stands in default without that many recent missed-installment entries, or when no winter plan stands in default but a balance-return entry with reason default was posted on any of the customer's plans within the 12 months before enrollment;
- **zero** otherwise.

The records read are the customer's Payment Arrangement plans — whether any Winter Protection Plan is in defaulted status — and the missed-installment and balance-return entries on all of the customer's plans. A window of 12 months before enrollment covers entries dated after the same calendar day 12 months earlier, up to and including the enrollment date.

## Truth table

| A Winter Protection Plan of the customer in defaulted status | Missed-installment entries on the customer's plans within 12 months | Balance-return entry with reason default within 12 months | Default share |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | 2 or more | Any | 30% |
| Yes | Fewer than 2 | Any | 15% |
| No | Any | Yes | 15% |
| No | Any | No | 0 |

title: Arrearage Management Program — Program Obligation of a Program Bill
content:
# Arrearage Management Program — Program Obligation of a Program Bill

**Rule.** For a program bill of an Arrearage Management Program plan, the forgiveness kind of Payment Arrangement, the program obligation is:

1. the monthly installment of the active Budget Billing plan, when the Electric Service Agreement carries an active Budget Billing plan;
2. the average current charges of the agreement's actual-read bills dated within the re-base window, rounded half-up to the cent, when the agreement carries no active Budget Billing plan, the program bill was an estimated-read bill and at least one actual-read bill is dated within that window;
3. the bill's current charges, in every other case.

The program bill is the Electric Service Agreement's most recent bill. Whether a bill is actual-read or estimated-read is shown on the bill record. The re-base window is the period of the agreement's bills read for a re-base, counted back from the booking day; a window of a number of months before booking covers bills dated after the same calendar day that many months earlier, up to and including the booking date. The average is the total current charges of the actual-read bills in the window divided by their number.

## Cases (hypothetical program bill, current charges $212.75)

| Active Budget Billing plan | Program bill read | Actual-read bills in the re-base window | Program obligation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes, monthly installment $148.00 | Any | Any | $148.00 |
| No | Estimated | $150.10, $162.40 and $171.05 | $483.55 divided by 3 is $161.1833, rounded half-up: $161.18 |
| No | Estimated | None | $212.75 |
| No | Actual | Any | $212.75 |

title: Arrearage Management Program Fact Sheet — Progress Credit
content:
# Arrearage Management Program Fact Sheet — Progress Credit

**Clause.** When withheld forgiveness on a program bill of an Arrearage Management Program plan, the forgiveness kind of Payment Arrangement, is posted as a catch-up, the progress credit is 10% when the forgiveness entries already posted on the plan number at least 0.9 times its installment count, 5% when they number at least 0.5 but less than 0.9 times that count, and zero otherwise. The entries counted are the plan's own forgiveness entries posted before the catch-up; the installment count is the count recorded on the plan.

## Reading the thresholds (hypothetical plan of 12 installments)

0.9 times 12 is 10.8 and 0.5 times 12 is 6.

| Forgiveness entries already posted | At least 10.8 | At least 6 | Progress credit |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | No | No | 0 |
| 6 | No | Yes | 5% |
| 10 | No | Yes | 5% |
| 11 | Yes | Yes | 10% |

title: Arrearage Management Program Re-Base Window Schedule
content:
# Arrearage Management Program Re-Base Window Schedule

**Schedule.** For a program bill of an Arrearage Management Program plan, the forgiveness kind of Payment Arrangement, the re-base window — the period of the agreement's bills read for a re-base, counted back from the booking day — is:

| Space heating on the Electric Service Agreement | Plan's enrolled date | Re-base window |
|---|---|---|
| Electric | Any | The 12 months before booking |
| Not electric | At least 6 whole calendar months before booking | The 3 months before booking |
| Not electric | Fewer than 6 whole calendar months before booking | The 6 months before booking |

Months between the plan's enrolled date and the booking day are counted in whole calendar months. A window of a number of months before booking covers bills dated after the same calendar day that many months earlier, up to and including the booking date.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical gas-heated agreement, plan enrolled January 15)

| Booking day | Whole calendar months since enrollment | Re-base window |
|---|---|---|
| July 14 | 5 | 6 months |
| July 15 | 6 | 3 months |

For an all-electric home the window is 12 months whatever the plan's enrolled date.

title: Payment Arrangement Reinstatement and Renegotiation Limits
content:
# Payment Arrangement Reinstatement and Renegotiation Limits

Two later changes are possible on some kinds of Payment Arrangement: putting a defaulted plan back into force (reinstatement) and changing the installment count of an active plan for a change in the customer's circumstances (renegotiation). The limits for each kind are:

| Arrangement kind | Reinstatements allowed | Days after the default to request reinstatement | Share of all missed installments to be paid before reinstatement | Renegotiations allowed | Ceiling on total installments after renegotiation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Payment Extension | 0 | 0 | 0% | 0 | 0 |
| Short-Term Installment Plan | 0 | 0 | 0% | 0 | 0 |
| Standard Deferred Payment Agreement | 1 | 30 | 100% | 1 | 9 |
| Extended Deferred Payment Agreement | 1 | 30 | 100% | 1 | 18 |
| Winter Protection Plan | 1 | 30 | 100% | 0 | 0 |
| Arrearage Management Program | 0 | 0 | 0% | 0 | 0 |
| Commercial Deferred Payment Agreement | 0 | 0 | 0% | 0 | 0 |

## Notes to the table

1. A reinstatement window of 0 days and a share of 0% mean the kind offers no reinstatement.
2. A renegotiation ceiling of 0 means the kind offers no renegotiation.
3. Reinstatement is offered on three kinds — the Standard Deferred Payment Agreement, the Extended Deferred Payment Agreement and the Winter Protection Plan — once each. Renegotiation is offered on the two deferred payment agreements, once each.
4. The share of missed installments is a fraction of all installments recorded as missed on the plan; 100% means every missed installment.

title: Payment Arrangement Reinstatement of a Defaulted Plan
content:
# Payment Arrangement Reinstatement of a Defaulted Plan

## Clauses in force

1. A defaulted Payment Arrangement plan may be reinstated only where the kind allows reinstatement (its reinstatements allowed is above zero) and the plan's reinstatements so far — the re-deferrals booked on it at reinstatement over its whole life — are below that number.
2. Reinstatement must be requested no later than the reinstatement window after the date the plan defaulted. The window is counted in calendar days from the day after the default date, and a request on the last day is accepted. The default date is the plan's latest status date, the date it moved to defaulted status.
3. A plan that cannot be reinstated stays defaulted, and its balance stays due on the service agreement.

## Retired clauses

- The former clause that before reinstatement the customer must have paid the kind's share of all installments recorded as missed, through payments posted to the service agreement after the default, is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis.
- The former clause that on reinstatement the plan returns to active, the missed-installment count restarts from zero, the returned balance is deferred into the plan again, and the remaining installments keep their numbers and amounts, is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis.

## Window cases (hypothetical, window of 30 days)

| Plan defaulted on | First day of the window | Last day of the window | Request made on | Inside the window |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| July 3 | July 4 | August 2 | August 2 | Yes — the last day is accepted |
| July 3 | July 4 | August 2 | August 3 | No |
| July 3 | July 4 | August 2 | July 3 | Yes — no later than the last day |

## Points of judgement

- A kind that allows no reinstatement keeps a defaulted plan defaulted.
- A plan already reinstated once, on a kind allowing one reinstatement, cannot be reinstated again.

title: Deferred Payment Agreement Reinstatement — Re-Deferral and Restoration Payment Calculation
content:
# Deferred Payment Agreement Reinstatement — Re-Deferral and Restoration Payment Calculation

This memorandum sets how the reinstatement re-deferral and the restoration payment are calculated when a defaulted Standard Deferred Payment Agreement or Extended Deferred Payment Agreement, the deferred payment agreement kinds of Payment Arrangement, is reinstated.

## 1. The returned balance

The reinstatement re-deferral starts from the returned balance, which is the amount of the latest balance-return entry with reason default on the plan — the plan balance that went back onto the service agreement when the plan defaulted.

## 2. The re-deferral and the restoration payment

- The **reinstatement re-deferral** is the returned balance times one minus the restoration share, rounded half-up to the cent.
- The **restoration payment** is the returned balance less the reinstatement re-deferral, so that the two together make up the returned balance to the cent.

## 3. The restoration share

The combined restoration share is the missed-installment share plus the returned-payment share plus the late-charge share, less the assistance relief; these are first added together into one share. The restoration share is the combined restoration share, a combined share below zero counting as zero, and it is applied once to the returned balance. A share or relief whose conditions are not met is zero. The standard restoration share is zero, so that the whole returned balance is booked back under the plan.

## 4. Account history

Account history read for a reinstatement is taken from the service agreement's records over the 12 months before the request. A window of a number of months before the request covers entries posted after the same calendar day that many months earlier, up to and including the request date.

## Worked example (hypothetical plan)

| Item | Figure |
|---|---|
| Latest balance-return entry with reason default | $1843.27, posted on the default date |
| Restoration share | The standard share of 0 |
| Reinstatement re-deferral | $1843.27 times one, rounded half-up to the cent: $1843.27 |
| Restoration payment | $1843.27 less the re-deferral of $1843.27: $0.00 |
| Account history read for a request dated September 18 | Entries posted after September 18 of the previous year, up to and including the request date |

**Rounding to the cent (hypothetical restoration share of 7%).** A returned balance of $1000.05 times 0.93 is $930.0465, so the re-deferral rounded half-up to the cent is $930.05, and the restoration payment is $1000.05 less $930.05, that is $70.00; the two together make up the $1000.05.

Where a plan has defaulted more than once, only the latest balance-return entry with reason default is the returned balance.

title: Payment Arrangement Renegotiated Installment — Calculation Sheet
content:
# Payment Arrangement Renegotiated Installment — Calculation Sheet

This sheet sets the new total installment count and the new regular installment when the schedule of an active Payment Arrangement plan is renegotiated.

## 1. The new count

The new total installment count is the renegotiation ceiling plus the billed installments not counted as used. The installments remaining are the new total installment count less the installments already billed, which is the renegotiation ceiling less the installments counted as used, so every remaining installment has its own installment number. The installments already billed are the installment billings recorded on the plan.

## 2. The renegotiation ceiling

The renegotiation ceiling is the kind's ceiling on total installments after renegotiation plus the winter stretch, plus the tenure months and plus the deposit months, less the history cut and less the default cut, all added together into one whole count. As standard, the renegotiation ceiling is the kind's ceiling on total installments after renegotiation, and every installment billed on the plan is counted as used.

## 3. The new regular installment

The regular installment for the installments not yet billed is the plan's remaining balance divided by the installments remaining, rounded down to the cent, with the final installment carrying the remainder.

## Worked sheet A (hypothetical Standard Deferred Payment Agreement, kind ceiling of 9)

| Line | Figure |
|---|---|
| Remaining balance under the plan | $1212.43 |
| Installments already billed | 4 |
| Installments counted as used | 4 |
| Renegotiation ceiling | 9 |
| New total installment count | 9 plus 0 not counted as used: 9 |
| Installments remaining | 9 less 4 billed: 5 (installments 5 to 9) |
| Regular installment | $1212.43 divided by 5 is $242.486, rounded down: $242.48 |
| Final installment (number 9) | $1212.43 less four regular installments of $242.48: $242.51 |

## Worked sheet B (same plan, hypothetically 3 of the 4 billed installments counted as used)

| Line | Figure |
|---|---|
| New total installment count | 9 plus 1 not counted as used: 10 |
| Installments remaining | 10 less 4 billed: 6, equal to 9 less 3 counted as used |
| Regular installment | $1212.43 divided by 6, rounded down to the cent: $202.07 |
| Final installment (number 10) | $1212.43 less five regular installments of $202.07: $202.08 |

title: Payment Arrangement Account History Standard — Restoration Review Window
content:
# Payment Arrangement Account History Standard — Restoration Review Window

**Standard.** When a defaulted Standard Deferred Payment Agreement or Extended Deferred Payment Agreement of the Payment Arrangement program is reinstated, the restoration review window — the period of the service agreement's account history read for the reinstatement — is set from the start date of the Electric Service Agreement and the returned-payment charges posted to it:

| Start date of the Electric Service Agreement | Returned-payment charge posted to the agreement within the 24 months before the request | Restoration review window |
|---|---|---|
| At least 120 months before the request | None | The 6 months before the request |
| At least 120 months before the request | One or more | The 9 months before the request |
| Fewer than 120 months before the request | Either | The 12 months before the request |

## Counting rules

- The number of months between the start date and the request is counted in whole calendar months.
- A window of a number of months before the request covers entries posted after the same calendar day that many months earlier, up to and including the request date. This applies both to the 24-month look-back for returned-payment charges and to the review window itself.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical agreement started March 20, 2015)

| Request dated | Whole calendar months since the start date | At least 120 |
|---|---|---|
| March 19, 2025 | 119 | No — window of 12 months |
| March 20, 2025 | 120 | Yes |

## Worked readings (hypothetical agreements)

1. Service since 2009, a returned-payment charge posted 20 months before the request: window of 9 months.
2. Service since 2009, the only returned-payment charge posted 30 months before the request: no charge within the 24 months, window of 6 months.
3. Service since 2019: window of 12 months whatever the returned-payment history.

title: Late Payment Charges and the Restoration of a Defaulted Payment Arrangement — Basis Q&A
content:
# Late Payment Charges and the Restoration of a Defaulted Payment Arrangement — Basis Q&A

**Rule.** When a defaulted Standard Deferred Payment Agreement or Extended Deferred Payment Agreement of the Payment Arrangement program is reinstated, the late-charge share is 6% when 6 or more late payment charges were posted to the Electric Service Agreement within the restoration review window, 3% when at least 3 but fewer than 6 were, and zero when fewer than 3 were. The restoration review window is the period of the agreement's account history read for the reinstatement; a window of a number of months before the request covers charges posted after the same calendar day that many months earlier, up to and including the request date.

## Questions the rule answers

**Which charges are counted?**
The late payment charges posted to the Electric Service Agreement's ledger within the restoration review window.

**What share applies at exactly 3 late payment charges?**
3% — the middle band starts at 3.

**What share applies at 5 late payment charges?**
3% — 5 is at least 3 and fewer than 6.

**What share applies at exactly 6 late payment charges?**
6% — the upper band starts at 6.

**What share applies at 2 late payment charges?**
Zero — fewer than 3.

| Late payment charges in the window | 0 | 2 | 3 | 5 | 6 | 9 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Late-charge share | 0 | 0 | 3% | 3% | 6% | 6% |

title: Payment Arrangement Credit Schedule — Missed-Installment Share on Reinstatement
content:
# Payment Arrangement Credit Schedule — Missed-Installment Share on Reinstatement

**Schedule.** When a defaulted Standard Deferred Payment Agreement or Extended Deferred Payment Agreement of the Payment Arrangement program is reinstated, the missed-installment share is:

| Missed-installment entries posted on the plan within the 6 months before the request | Missed-installment share |
|---|---|
| Three or more | 15% |
| Exactly two | 10% |
| Fewer than two | 0 |

The count reads the plan's own history: its missed-installment entries, each posted on the day after the cure period of the installment ended unpaid. A window of 6 months before the request covers entries posted after the same calendar day 6 months earlier, up to and including the request date. Missed-installment entries posted before that window have aged out of it and do not count, even though they remain on the plan.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical request dated July 10)

| Entry posted on | Inside the 6 months before the request |
|---|---|
| January 10 | No — the window covers entries posted after January 10 |
| January 11 | Yes |
| July 10 | Yes — the request date is included |

## Worked readings (hypothetical plans, request dated July 10)

| Missed entries on the plan | Of which posted after January 10 | Share |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | 3 | 15% |
| 4 | 2 | 10% |
| 2 | 1 | 0 |
| 3 | 0 | 0 |

title: Payment Arrangement Decision Table — Returned-Payment Share on Reinstatement
content:
# Payment Arrangement Decision Table — Returned-Payment Share on Reinstatement

**Rule.** When a defaulted Standard Deferred Payment Agreement or Extended Deferred Payment Agreement of the Payment Arrangement program is reinstated, the returned-payment share is set by the returned-payment charges posted to the Electric Service Agreement within the restoration review window — the period of the agreement's account history read for the reinstatement.

| Returned-payment charges posted to the Electric Service Agreement within the restoration review window | Returned-payment share |
|---|---|
| Two or more | 10% |
| Exactly one | 5% |
| None | 0 |

A returned-payment charge is the charge the Electric Service Agreement's ledger records when a payment is returned unpaid. A window of a number of months before the request covers charges posted after the same calendar day that many months earlier, up to and including the request date.

## Input — judgement — output (hypothetical agreements)

| Charges in the review window | Judgement | Share |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | None | 0 |
| 1 | Exactly one | 5% |
| 2 | Two or more | 10% |
| 5 | Two or more | 10% |

A returned-payment charge posted before the review window began does not enter the count.

title: Payment Extension Returned-Payment Share — Decision Table
content:
# Payment Extension Returned-Payment Share — Decision Table

**Rule.** For a Payment Extension — the single-installment kind of Payment Arrangement — enrolled on a residential agreement under disconnection notice, the returned-payment share is read from the returned-payment charges posted to any of the customer's Electric Service Agreements within the 12 months before enrollment:

| Returned-payment charges on any of the customer's Electric Service Agreements within the 12 months | Returned-payment share |
|---|---|
| Two or more | 10% |
| Exactly one | 5% |
| None | 0 |

All of the customer's agreements are counted together, not only the agreement under notice. A window of 12 months before enrollment covers charges posted after the same calendar day 12 months earlier, up to and including the enrollment date.

## Input — judgement — output (hypothetical customer with two agreements)

| Charges within the window | Judgement | Share |
|---|---|---|
| One on the home agreement, one on a second agreement | Two in total | 10% |
| One on the second agreement only | Exactly one | 5% |
| One posted 13 months before enrollment | Outside the window | 0 |

title: Security Deposit Treatment on Winter Protection Plan Reinstatement
content:
# Security Deposit Treatment on Winter Protection Plan Reinstatement

**Rule.** When a defaulted Winter Protection Plan of the Payment Arrangement program is reinstated, the deposit treatment applies when a Security Deposit in held status on the agreement secures it:

1. When the held deposit holds at least $200.00, the deposit stands behind the returned-payment risk and the winter returned-payment share is left out, so the good-faith share is the winter missed-installment share alone.
2. When a held deposit holds more than zero but less than $200.00, the combined winter share is multiplied by 0.75.
3. When no deposit is held on the agreement, the combined winter share is used as it stands.

The record read is the Security Deposit on the same service agreement as the winter plan: whether it is in held status and the amount it holds.

## Cases (hypothetical shares: winter missed-installment share 8%, winter returned-payment share 6%, combined 14%)

| Security Deposit on the agreement | Treatment | Good-faith share |
|---|---|---|
| Held, $250.00 | Returned-payment share left out | 8% |
| Held, $200.00 | Returned-payment share left out — at least $200.00 | 8% |
| Held, $199.99 | Combined share multiplied by 0.75 | 14% times 0.75: 10.5% |
| Assessed but not held, or none | Combined share as it stands | 14% |

title: Winter Protection Plan Reinstatement — Seasonal Desk Card
content:
# Winter Protection Plan Reinstatement — Seasonal Desk Card

**Terms.** A defaulted Winter Protection Plan, the seasonal kind of Payment Arrangement for households with electric space heating, is reinstated at the customer's request on the terms of this card, which refine the reinstatement rule of the Payment Arrangement program for winter plans; the reinstatement window, the number of reinstatements allowed and the requirement that the request fall inside the window are unchanged.

- On reinstatement the winter plan returns to active, its missed-installment count restarts from zero, its remaining installments keep their numbers and amounts, and the balance booked back under it is the winter re-deferral rather than the whole returned balance.
- For a reinstated winter plan, the amount booked back into the plan and credited off the service agreement's collectible balance is the winter re-deferral, not the remaining unbilled plan balance.
- Before the winter plan is reinstated the customer must have paid the kind's required share of all its installments recorded as missed and the whole winter good-faith payment, through payments posted to the service agreement after the default.

## Recording the reinstatement — `reinstate_winter_protection_plan_6f5d50f4`

**What the tool does.** It reinstates one Winter Protection Plan that is in default, putting it back into force today. The plan identified by the reference number is set back to active status with today's date as its latest status change, and the balance held under it is set to the re-deferred amount given, which from then on is repaid by the plan's remaining installments. The installment count and regular installment on file are left as they are. Afterwards a lookup of the plan shows it active, dated today, with the new balance remaining.

**How it is invoked.** This is an agent-side tool. The agent unlocks it with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool` and then calls it with `call_agent_discoverable_tool`, naming `reinstate_winter_protection_plan_6f5d50f4`.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `arrangement_id` | The reference number of the Winter Protection Plan being reinstated, as returned by the payment arrangement lookup | Identifier |
| `redeferred_amount` | The balance placed back under the plan at reinstatement | US dollars with 2 decimal places, a plain number such as 327.60 with no currency sign; stored rounded half-up to the cent |

**Return.** A text receipt: "Winter Protection Plan <arrangement_id> reinstated: status active as of <YYYY-MM-DD>, balance remaining <amount> USD." The date is today's date and the amount carries 2 decimal places. Receiving this receipt means the reinstatement is recorded.

## Illustration (hypothetical values)

A call with `arrangement_id` ARR-0004 and `redeferred_amount` 327.60 on a day dated 2026-02-10 returns: "Winter Protection Plan ARR-0004 reinstated: status active as of 2026-02-10, balance remaining 327.60 USD."

title: Winter Protection Plan Re-Deferral and Good-Faith Payment — Calculation Memo
content:
# Winter Protection Plan Re-Deferral and Good-Faith Payment — Calculation Memo

This memorandum sets the winter re-deferral and the winter good-faith payment when a defaulted Winter Protection Plan, the seasonal kind of Payment Arrangement, is reinstated.

## 1. The returned balance

The winter plan's returned balance is the amount of its latest balance-return entry with reason default — the plan balance that went back onto the service agreement when the plan defaulted.

## 2. The re-deferral and the good-faith payment

- The **winter re-deferral** is the returned balance times one minus the winter good-faith share, rounded half-up to the cent.
- The **winter good-faith payment** is the returned balance less the winter re-deferral, so that the two together make up the returned balance to the cent.

## 3. The winter good-faith share

The combined winter share is the winter missed-installment share plus the winter returned-payment share, added together into one share. The winter good-faith share is the combined winter share, applied once to the returned balance. The standard winter good-faith share is zero, so that the whole returned balance is booked back under the winter plan.

## 4. Review period

As standard, the agreement's returned payments are reviewed over the 12 months before the request. A window of a number of months before the request covers entries dated after the same calendar day that many months earlier, up to and including the request date.

## Worked example (hypothetical winter plan)

| Line | Figure |
|---|---|
| Latest balance-return entry with reason default | $642.18 |
| Winter good-faith share | The standard share of 0 |
| Winter re-deferral | $642.18 times one, rounded half-up to the cent: $642.18 |
| Winter good-faith payment | $642.18 less the re-deferral of $642.18: $0.00 |
| Returned payments reviewed for a request dated January 22 | Those posted after January 22 of the previous year, up to and including January 22 |

**Rounding to the cent (hypothetical good-faith share of 9%).** A returned balance of $642.18 times 0.91 is $584.3838, so the winter re-deferral rounded half-up to the cent is $584.38, and the winter good-faith payment is $642.18 less $584.38, that is $57.80; the two together make up the $642.18.

The winter review window is the period over which the agreement's returned-payment charges are reviewed for the reinstatement.

The returned-payment charges on the ledger of the Electric Service Agreement that carries the winter plan, posted within the winter review window.

**What applies with two or more?** 6%.

**What applies when the only returned-payment charge was posted before the window began?** Zero — it is not within the window.

| Returned-payment charges in the window | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Winter returned-payment share | 0 | 3% | 6% | 6% |

title: Payment Arrangement Winter Stretch on Renegotiated Schedules
content:
# Payment Arrangement Winter Stretch on Renegotiated Schedules

**Clause.** When the installment schedule of an active Payment Arrangement plan is renegotiated, the winter stretch is:

- **4 months** when the Electric Service Agreement's space heating is electric, its most recent bill is a winter-season bill, and it carries an active medical protection under the Medical and Life-Support Protections;
- **2 months** when the space heating is electric and the most recent bill is a winter-season bill, but no medical protection is active on it;
- **zero** in every other case — heating that is not electric, or a most recent bill that is not a winter-season bill.

The records read are the space heating recorded on the Electric Service Agreement, the season of its most recent bill by bill date, and the status of any medical protection on the same agreement.

## Truth table

| Electric space heating | Most recent bill is a winter-season bill | Active medical protection | Winter stretch |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | Yes | 4 months |
| Yes | Yes | No | 2 months |
| Yes | No (summer season) | Yes | 0 |
| Yes | No (summer season) | No | 0 |
| No | Yes | Yes | 0 |
| No | Yes | No | 0 |
| No | No | Either | 0 |

## Hypothetical readings

1. An all-electric home whose latest bill, dated January 8, is a winter-season bill, with a medical protection active on the agreement: 4 months.
2. The same home with the medical protection expired before the renegotiation: 2 months.
3. A gas-heated home in January with an active medical protection: 0.
